# Zan Language

> Zan is an independent, statically typed language with C#-style syntax, LLVM native AOT compilation and ARC. It is not a .NET implementation. This site publishes static HTML, Markdown and a full-text bundle from the same documentation sources.

Reviewed against repository sources: 2026-11-11. Match facts to the installed SDK version. Source paths cited in chapters are repository/SDK provenance, not fabricated public source URLs.

## Read first

- [Documentation index](./docs/index.md): learning order, topic map and machine-readable resources.
- [Complete documentation](./llms-full.txt): all chapters, package catalog and English agent guide in one text file; use when context allows, otherwise read individual chapters.
- [English agent guide](./agent-guide.md): key semantic differences, local SDK discovery, MCP setup and verification.
- [Understanding Zan](./docs/overview.md): language goals, application scope, compilation model and licensing.
- [Quickstart](./docs/quickstart.md): SDK setup, a complete program, compilation and multi-file projects.

## Language semantics

- [Syntax and program structure](./docs/language.md): declarations, namespaces, control flow, exceptions and resource scopes.
- [Types and abstractions](./docs/types.md): primitive types, classes, structs, interfaces, generics, delegates, properties, tuples and patterns.
- [Memory and resources](./docs/memory.md): ARC, weak references, cycles, null, UTF-8 byte semantics, collection aliasing and explicit cleanup.
- [Async and concurrency](./docs/async.md): async result types, await, Task.Run/Spawn, scheduler configuration, cancellation and synchronization.
- [Native interoperability](./docs/interop.md): DllImport, C ABI, struct layout, pointers and conditional compilation.

## Libraries, platforms and tools

- [Standard library and application development](./docs/libraries.md): compiler builtins versus core library versus extension packages; GUI, networking, data, AI and games.
- [Complete package catalog](./docs/packages.md): generated from current package manifests and actual source namespace declarations; maturity and licenses are separate facts.
- [Toolchain and delivery](./docs/tooling.md): zanc flags, package discovery, diagnostics, IDE, LSP, DAP and publishing.
- [Platform boundaries](./docs/platforms.md): compilation, execution, GUI and packaging are listed independently.
- [AI development workflow](./docs/ai.md): how to retrieve context, query real APIs and verify results.

## Machine-readable resources

- [Document manifest](./docs/manifest.json): versioned schema, source references, descriptions, URLs and SHA-256 of each Markdown chapter.
- [Package metadata](./docs/packages.json): current manifest metadata and declared namespaces; not a download or production-readiness guarantee.
- [Search corpus](./docs/search.json): searchable chapter text matching the published documentation.

## Official distribution

- [IDE / SDK and packages](https://github.com/joyspinch/zanlang): inspect the current README and available files before choosing downloads.
- [SDK AI onboarding](https://github.com/joyspinch/zanlang/blob/main/AI_README.md)
- [Feedback](https://github.com/joyspinch/zanlang/issues)

Do not infer Zan behavior from C# or NuGet. In particular, inspect UTF-8 strings, collection aliases, ARC/resource cleanup, async result types, supported boxing and target capabilities. Ordinary SDK users do not need to build the compiler. Query the installed API index or MCP tools, then compile and run the actual project. These files enable retrieval; they do not automatically train a model or guarantee that every AI client reads every chapter.
